sections.heading: What is the Prefix Sum Pattern?
sections.content: A prefix sum array stores the running total of elements up to each index. Once built in O(n), the sum of any range [l, r] is answered in O(1) using one subtraction. The same idea extends to counts, XOR, products and 2D grids. A Difference Array is the reverse trick: it makes many range updates cheap, then one pass rebuilds the final array.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Many queries for the sum of a subarray or range
Count subarrays with a given sum (especially with negative numbers)
Find a subarray with sum divisible by K or equal to K
Compare the left part and right part of an array (pivot index)
Many range updates such as add x to every index from l to r
Range sums on a 2D matrix
The array does not change between queries (static data)

rows.answer: Rebuild with a prefix sum in O(n)

sections.heading: Template 1: Build a Prefix Sum Array
Why Use Size n + 1
items: prefix[0] = 0 represents the empty prefix
It removes the special case when l = 0
Range sum of a[l..r] is always prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l]
Use LongArray when sums can exceed Int range (about 2.1 billion)

sections.heading: Template 2: Prefix Sum + HashMap (Subarray Sum Equals K)
The Core Idea Behind Prefix Sum + HashMap
sections.content: If prefix[j] - prefix[i] = k, then the subarray between i and j sums to k. So while scanning, for each current prefix sum you look up how many earlier prefixes equal (current - k). Always put count[0] = 1 first so subarrays starting at index 0 are counted.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Forgetting count[0] = 1 (or firstSeen[0] = -1) in the HashMap version
Off by one: range sum is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l], not prefix[r] - prefix[l]
Integer overflow: use Long for large sums or products
Negative remainder in Kotlin: % can return a negative value, so use ((x % k) + k) % k
Using a sliding window when the array has negative numbers
Updating the HashMap before checking it (this counts the same prefix with itself)
In a difference array, forgetting the extra slot at index r + 1

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Prefix sum turns any range sum into one subtraction
Use size n + 1 with prefix[0] = 0 to avoid edge cases
Prefix sum + HashMap counts subarrays with a target sum, even with negatives
Equal prefix remainders mean the subarray sum is divisible by K
Difference arrays make many range updates O(1) each
2D prefix sums use inclusion-exclusion for rectangle queries
